notes:
- **A progress dialog for exports.** A Quick Export or an Export panel run that takes more than half a second shows what it is doing and how far along it is, photograph by photograph, with a **Cancel** that stops it where it is and keeps what was already written. [Exporting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/export/#run-and-stop).
- **Export a TIFF or EXR without its layers.** The Export panel has a **Layers** switch when the edit carries export layers: **Left out** writes the picture alone, without unticking each layer in the edit. Presets remember it. [Exporting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/export/#export-layers).
- **iPhone ProRAW exports in a fraction of the memory.** A ProRAW photograph is now read a tile at a time as the export reaches each part of it, instead of being developed whole first, with exactly the same pixels as before. A 48 MP ProRAW's export starts from about a quarter of the memory it took, and reads in about half the time. [Exporting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/export/#memory-and-large-exports).
- **Detail Equalizer.** A new **EQUALIZER** fold in Detail raises or lowers contrast at five scales of detail, from the finest texture to broad shapes, like Tone Equalizer does for brightness. Lift the middle scales while calming the finest, and click a band's eye to see exactly which detail it holds. Texture and Clarity stay where they were. [Detail](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/detail/#equalizer).
- **Line profile.** A new scope plots brightness, and the red, green and blue channels if you like, along a path you draw across the photograph a point at a time, then edit point by point. A radius averages that many of the photograph's pixels each side of the path, and the band button shows what it reads in red. Point at the plot and the place is marked on the path, and the other way around. [Scopes](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/#line-profile).
- **Pick a depth for a layer.** A layer's Depth mask can now take one slice of depth instead of a ramp from far to near. Click the eyedropper beside the depth eye, then click the subject: the layer takes the subject's distance, easing off nearer and farther, and Shift-click widens the slice. Drag its edges and falloff on the depth histogram. Each layer keeps its own slice, so several layers can each work on a different distance. In Develop's adjustment layers, Color Sets and Finish layers. [Local adjustments](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/#local-adjustments).
- **Color pairs in Recolor.** Pick two colors on the photograph, a sky and a sunset, and change their relationship: turn their hues apart or together, move saturation from one to the other, widen or narrow the brightness between them, on a small color wheel you can drag. Each pair folds to its two colors while you work another. [Recolor](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/recolor/#color-pairs).
- **Inspect a pixel.** The viewer's new crosshair button traces any point through your edit: every node on its path with the color it receives and hands on, how much a layer's mask lets through there, and the final color. The panel opens in its own column beside the photograph, left of the Adjustments panel or, with a click, right of the thumbnail strip, and folds the Library and the strip away while it is open. From the same panel, or a node's menu in Graph, **Map** shows where a node changes the whole picture and **Isolate** shows only what it adds. [Viewing](https://www.heeler.app/docs/image-viewport/#inspect-a-pixel).
- **Big exports fit in less memory.** A full-size export renders the photograph in horizontal strips and writes each strip into the file as it goes, so even a 48 MP photograph with heavy edits exports within a phone's memory, with the same pixels as before. Heeler also hands memory back to the system sooner, which keeps large exports lighter on any computer. [Exporting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/export/).
- **Exports of light edits take about half the time.** An export that fits in memory now renders in one piece instead of in strips, and choosing how to split a heavy one no longer costs a tenth of a second before it starts. [Exporting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/export/).
- **JPEG exports encode about three times faster.** Exports now use the same fast encoder as the canvas's frames: a 24 MP JPEG encodes in under a tenth of a second. At the default quality of 92 the files are the same size as before; at 95 and above they are larger, because the old encoder stopped adding detail there and its 100 was really about 95, where the new one keeps what each step of quality asks for. [Exporting](https://www.heeler.app/docs/export/).
- **Depth refinement for an export takes half the time, and none the second time.** An edit that uses the Depth Map refines its depth at full size for the export, now across all of the computer's cores, and keeps the result, so the next export of the same edit starts straight away. [Depth Map](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-map/).
- **Zooming to 1:1 is ready sooner.** A photograph that stays open a moment is decoded at full size in the background, so the first zoom to 1:1, and its export, no longer wait for that decode, which took several seconds for some RAW files. [Viewing](https://www.heeler.app/docs/image-viewport/).
- **RAW files open faster.** The demosaic that turns a camera's sensor pattern into a picture now runs across all of the computer's cores, for every Bayer camera and for Fujifilm's X-Trans, with exactly the same result as before. And with Highlights on **Blend**, which develops a clipped RAW twice and mixes the two, both develops now run at once. Measured against 2026.5.5: a Fujifilm RAF opens in about 40 percent of the time, a 61 MP Sony file in under 60 percent, Panasonic, GoPro and iPhone ProRAW files in about 70 percent. [Source](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/source/).
- **A crop no longer drops the depth map or shrinks the preview.** A crop, or the crop tool showing the whole frame, needed a depth map of its own, which Heeler did not read; cutting the depth map to a crop could also be refused as if no memory were left, dropping the preview to 1024 pixels. Either way a layer limited by its Depth mask lost that limit until the map was read again: a radial brightening meant for the subject lit its whole ellipse. The depth map is now read from the photograph before the crop and cut to each crop, so cropping and the crop tool never wait for it to be read again, and nothing flashes. [Depth Map](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/depth-map/).
- **Polishing a selection after a crop.** Refine edge and the matte brush solved the edge on the cropped picture but kept it as if it covered the whole photograph, so the crop was applied twice and the matte landed zoomed in and off the subject; a flip or a turn did the same. The matte now lands where it was solved, and Apply's full-resolution pass follows it. A matte made before this fix keeps its old place: undo it and polish again. Polishing a photograph whose crop is rotated, or that is warped or corrected for lens distortion, says it cannot yet rather than placing the matte wrong. [Masks and selections](https://www.heeler.app/docs/finish/masks-selections/).
- **A Finish layer's Depth mask computes the depth map by itself.** With nothing else in the edit reading depth, turning on a Finish layer's Depth mask never asked for the depth map, so its Levels sat over an empty histogram and the mask had no depth to shape. It now asks for the map the way a Develop layer's does. [Masks and selections](https://www.heeler.app/docs/finish/masks-selections/).
- **Grain shows in the canvas.** With GPU previews on, the canvas passed over a Grain set in its section as if it were zero, and over an Unsharp set in Detail too, so the fitted view showed neither while 1:1, the thumbnail and the export did. Both now render in every view. A reduced preview also drew a frame-sized grain fainter than the export shows it at that size; it now draws it as strong. [Grain](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/grain/).
- **Recolor's Neutral guard sits under the curve.** The guard and its strip now come after the routing grid and curve they act on, with Smoothing above. [Recolor](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/recolor/).
- **Curve editors fit a narrow panel.** In Recolor, Tone Equalizer, Black & White and Color Sets, the eyedropper now sits above the curve's left corner with the Layout menu beside it, leaving the row under the curve to the point's numbers and the curve type. Recolor's BY and ADJUST menus each take a row of their own. [Recolor](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/recolor/).
- **Click a layer again to fold it.** Clicking the selected adjustment layer's name in Develop now folds its controls, and clicking again opens them. In Finish, with **Expand settings on select** on, clicking the selected layer's row does the same. [Adjustment layers](https://www.heeler.app/docs/adjustments/), [Finish](https://www.heeler.app/docs/finish/#settings-that-open-and-close).
